items.prompt: The fruit pattern keeps going. Which fruit comes next?

figure.alt: A row of fruit: apple, apple, banana, apple, apple, banana, apple, then an empty space.

options.why: A banana comes after two apples. The new group has only one apple so far.
There are no pears in this pattern.
There are no oranges in this pattern.
There are no cherries in this pattern.

hints: Look for the part that repeats.
Say the fruits aloud in groups of three: apple, apple, banana.
The 7th fruit starts a new group. Which fruit is second in every group?
items.explanation: The part that repeats is apple, apple, banana. The 7th fruit is the first apple of a new group, so the next fruit is the second apple.

solution.say: The pattern repeats in groups of three.
Split the row into groups.
solution.show: apple, apple, banana | apple, apple, banana | apple, ?

solution.say: Every group has two apples before the banana. The new group has one apple so far, so the next fruit is an apple.

items.prompt: Mia threads beads in this pattern. She threads 12 beads in all. How many beads are blue?

figure.alt: Beads on a string: red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue. The pattern repeats: 1 red bead, then 2 blue beads.

options.why: 4 is the number of red beads.
6 is half of 12, but each group has more blue beads than red ones.
Count the groups again. 12 beads make 4 groups of 3.
Not every bead is blue. Each group has 1 red bead.

hints: Find the group of beads that repeats.
Each group is red, blue, blue. Count how many groups fit in 12 beads.
Count in 3s up to 12: 3, 6, 9, 12.
items.explanation: 12 beads make 4 groups of red, blue, blue. Each group has 2 blue beads, so there are 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8 blue beads.

solution.say: One group is red, blue, blue. That is 3 beads.
Count in 3s to 12: 3, 6, 9, 12. So there are 4 groups.
Each group has 2 blue beads.

items.prompt: Tom builds staircases with blocks. A staircase with 1 step uses 1 block. With 2 steps it uses 3 blocks. With 3 steps it uses 6 blocks. With 4 steps it uses 10 blocks. How many blocks does a staircase with 5 steps use?

figure.alt: Blocks needed for staircases with 1, 2, 3 and 4 steps: 1, 3, 6 and 10. The number for 5 steps is missing.

options.why: 11 adds only 1. The jumps get bigger each time.
12 adds 2. The jumps get bigger each time.
13 adds 3, but the last jump was already 4.
14 adds 4, the same as the last jump. Each jump is 1 more than the one before.

hints: Look at how much the number grows each time.
Write down the jumps: from 1 to 3, from 3 to 6, from 6 to 10.
The jumps are +2, +3 and +4. What will the next jump be?
items.explanation: The numbers grow by 2, then 3, then 4, so the next jump is 5. A staircase with 5 steps uses 10 + 5 = 15 blocks.

solution.say: Find how much each staircase grows.
The jumps are 2, 3 and 4. Each jump is 1 more than the one before.
The next jump is 5.
You can also see it as a new column of 5 blocks for the new step.

items.prompt: Ani menyusun jeruk dalam beberapa baris. Baris pertama ada 2 jeruk. Baris kedua ada 4 jeruk. Baris ketiga ada 6 jeruk. Berapa jeruk di baris ke-5?

figure.alt: Tiga baris jeruk: baris pertama 2 jeruk, baris kedua 4 jeruk, baris ketiga 6 jeruk.

options.why: 20 adalah jumlah jeruk di 4 baris pertama.
30 adalah jumlah semua jeruk di 5 baris.

hints: Lihat berapa jeruk bertambah dari satu baris ke baris berikutnya.
Setiap baris bertambah 2 jeruk. Lanjutkan polanya.
Hitung dulu isi baris ke-4, yaitu 6 + 2.
items.explanation: Setiap baris bertambah 2 jeruk: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Jadi baris ke-5 berisi 10 jeruk.

solution.say: Cari aturannya. Dari 2 ke 4 tambah 2, dari 4 ke 6 tambah 2.
Lanjutkan sampai baris ke-5.
Baris ke-5 berisi 10 jeruk.

items.prompt: A frog starts at 0 on a number line. It jumps 3 each time. Which number will the frog land on?

figure.alt: A number line from 0 to 20. The frog jumps from 0 to 3, then from 3 to 6, then from 6 to 9.

options.why: 10 is 9 + 1. The frog always jumps 3, not 1.
Count on in 3s from 9: 12, 15. The frog jumps over 14.
Count in 3s from 0. 17 is not on the list.

hints: The frog only lands on some numbers.
Count in 3s from 0: 0, 3, 6, 9 and keep going.
After 9 the frog lands on 12. Keep counting in 3s.
items.explanation: The frog lands on 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15 and 18. Of the four numbers, only 15 is on this list.

solution.say: The frog jumps 3 each time, so it lands on the numbers you say when you count in 3s.
Keep going.
15 is on the list. 10, 14 and 17 are not.

items.prompt: What is the missing number in this pattern?

figure.alt: Stones with the numbers 1, 2, 4, 7, 11, then a blank stone, then 22.

hints: Look at the jumps between the numbers.
From 1 to 2 is +1. From 2 to 4 is +2. Keep going.
The jumps are +1, +2, +3, +4. What is the next jump?
items.explanation: The jumps grow by 1 each time: +1, +2, +3, +4, +5, +6. So the missing number is 11 + 5 = 16, and 16 + 6 = 22 checks out.

solution.say: Write the jump between each pair of numbers.
The jumps are +1, +2, +3, +4.
The next jump is +5.
Check: the jump after that is +6.

items.prompt: Ken writes 1, 2, 3 again and again. He writes 10 numbers in all. What do the 10 numbers add up to?

figure.alt: Ten circles. The first six show 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3. The last four are empty.

hints: Find the group that repeats and its total.
1 + 2 + 3 = 6. How many full groups fit in 10 numbers?
Three full groups use 9 numbers. What is the 10th number?
items.explanation: Ten numbers are 3 full groups of 1, 2, 3 and then one more 1. That is 6 + 6 + 6 + 1 = 19.

solution.say: One group is 1, 2, 3. Its total is 6.
Three groups use 9 numbers. The 10th number starts a new group, so it is 1.
Add it all up.

items.prompt: Lila makes squares in a row with sticks. 1 square uses 4 sticks. 2 squares use 7 sticks. 3 squares use 10 sticks. How many sticks does she need for 5 squares?

head: Squares in a row
Sticks
figure.alt: A table: 1 square uses 4 sticks, 2 squares use 7 sticks, 3 squares use 10 sticks. The number of sticks for 5 squares is unknown.

hints: How many more sticks does each new square need?
From 4 to 7 is +3, and from 7 to 10 is +3. A new square shares one side.
Find the number of sticks for 4 squares first.
items.explanation: Each new square shares a side with the square before it, so it needs only 3 more sticks. 4 squares use 13 sticks and 5 squares use 16 sticks.

solution.say: Each new square needs 3 more sticks because one side is shared.
Add 3 for the 4th square.
Add 3 again for the 5th square.

items.prompt: Fill the grid with the numbers 1 to 3. Every row and every column must have each number once.
hints: Find a row or a column with only one empty box.
Look at which numbers are already there. Which one is missing?
Check the row and the column together.
items.explanation: Every row and column has each number once. For example, the first row is 3, 1, 2.
